result.summary:
Terrain fix round 2, continued on wf/terrain-r2b. The branch was cut from wf/terrain-r2 and has 11 commits on top of it, 8f794c1 to 9267b04. Nothing was pushed and the worktree is clean.

Two data problems were fixed and the data rebuilt with the committed tools:
1. The r2 WIP commit had shipped a partial landuse merge (40 of 56 tiles). The landuse now comes from one Overpass endpoint and one database state (ovp.dresel.systems North America, timestamp_osm_base 2026-11-19T21:22:20Z, all 56 tiles, 2,713 elements, sha recorded in refs/cache/osm_landuse/SOURCES.json).
2. The r2 query printed relations with 'out tags geom', which returns no member geometry, so all 59 multipolygon relations (for example 280 Metro Center, Serramonte Auto Row, the Gateway at Millbrae Station, the Kinder Morgan Brisbane Terminal) produced no polygon. The relation half of the query now uses 'out body geom'. Result: 2,713 polygons covering 144.4 km2, and 26.2 % of the NLCD-24 texels are commercial.

Other r2b changes:
- truth-r1-T4: ring 3 of the mesh is now 24 x step on the high tier and 36 x step on the low tier (was 48 x). The r2 prefilter is sigma 15 m. The rms gate now uses a 20,000-point r2 sample, so it can fail; the earlier 1.6k sample was lucky (sigma 30 gives 6.02 m on the 20k sample, over the 6 m gate). The drawn far mesh has its own error gate.
- truth-r1-T7: barren upland is now measured on two Landsat 9 SR sites (Permanente quarry and the Pleasanton gravel pits), with BOX_ONLY so each box contributes only its own class.
- look-r1-look-3: under motorway ribbon coverage the shading normal is now level, in both renderers (GLSL and TSL, using normalWorldGeometry to avoid a node cycle). The root cause of the dark blots was the 10-30 m DEM smearing fill crowns, which left carriageways on 25-46 % mesh slopes facing away from the 11 deg sun (N.L < 0).
- Docs: terrain.md and ATTRIBUTION.md updated, plus a stale ring-3 comment in terrain.js.

Renders: the phone artifact was rebuilt from a8a55ce (the relation-fixed data). It produced 20 high-tier stills at 1600x900 using the round-1 reviewer's cameras, 3 low-tier stills, and 2 old-renderer (live.html) stills. All were taken under the shared render lock and I looked at each one. The output folder has before/after pairs, crops for each finding, fog A/B pairs, and overlays checking the OSM commercial mask against the slabs.

Report file: the task asked for wf/terrain/r2/REPORT.md, but the harness refuses report .md files from subagents. The report is therefore this summary plus dispositions, checks, renders and open_questions.

Barren upland rests on two Landsat sites (479 lit pixels). More inland quarries would strengthen that palette entry.

dispositions.reason: Root cause: the bank rule forced height() up to level + 0.5 + 0.12 d within 400 m of every OSM ring. Since r2 it lifts only ground below level + 0.5 m within 45 m, fades out by 60 m and has no cone. A check_terrain gate (lakeBanks) requires |height - demY| = 0 beyond 60 m. HEAD probes: every reviewer point now matches 3DEP (San Andreas 109.38, was +49.5; below the dam 49.90, was +59.3; Lake Merced 5.28, was 30.75; I-280 123.55). Remaining lifts: San Andreas 0.0070 km2 (max +8.3 m), Upper Crystal Springs 0, Lake Merced <= 0.48 m, and the Lower Crystal Springs dam face (open question). Renders cmp_w2_merced and cmp_w1_sanandreas show natural banks.

Since r2 there are airfield mesh patches at the finest step around the NASR runways. The traffic floor is meshY/floorAt: the same lattice and triangle interpolation as the drawn mesh for the tier step. 5,173 runway points at steps 15 and 30 lie on the drawn triangles within 1 cm. Drawn surface vs height() is within 0.57 m (high) and 0.89 m (low) at 11 airfields (DVO, CCR, LVK, OAK, HAF among them). Gates floor_15 and floor_30 compare against the built mesh. Invariants show no vert.ground or vert.below events.
Outside the rings there is no edge clamp any more: floorAt uses the NASR field elevation for airfields beyond the rings, otherwise GROUND_Y. C83 is 22.93 (old clamp 58.42) and O69 26.5 (old 38.72).

Summit vertices from the raw 1-arcsecond DEM (r2) keep named East Bay and Marin peaks drawn within 6 m (Mt Diablo +0.02 m); these are gated. In r2b: ring 3 at 24 x step (high) and 36 x step (low) instead of 48 x; drawn far-mesh rms gated at 16.29/36.00 m against bounds of 20/40; r2 prefilter sigma 15 m. The r2 rms gate now uses 20,000 points and gives 5.59 m against the 6 m gate (sigma 30 would give 6.02 m, which fails). The old 1.6k sample sat at the 3rd percentile of its own bootstrap. height() at named r2 peaks stays within 40 m (Grizzly -32.5 m is the 120 m lattice); the drawn summit uses the raw maximum.

floorAt returns GROUND_Y only where flatW >= 1 (the shipped flat zone) and the drawn surface everywhere else. At the Millbrae hillside (-2700, 1540) it gives 40.20/40.07 m against DEM 40.30 (was 3.0).

r2 added a fine inner city bake (CITYFINE_RECT) over the 28L/R climb and approach corridors: 2.05 m/texel on high, 1.03 m on ultra, 4.1 m on low/phone. The comment states the phone texel size. Renders crops_look-8 and after_low_* show resolved houses.

Class 31 is split at DEM 20 m (I). Barren lowland keeps the salt-works palette. Barren upland is measured from Landsat 9 SR on two inland sites, the Permanente quarry and the Pleasanton gravel pits (479 lit pixels, BOX_ONLY so each box contributes only its own class): 0.1298/0.1124/0.0766, against 0.352/0.318/0.270 for the salt pans. Documented in terrain.md section 5; the representativeness question is in open_questions.
terrain.md section 3 is corrected to about 0.14 m (0.65 m without the realisation shift). It cites NGS GEOID18 N = -32.638 m at the ARP; the geoid answer is cached under refs/cache/geoid/.

The commercial slab archetype is drawn only where OSM maps landuse=commercial/retail/industrial (regionC.B > 0.5, observed, ODbL). NLCD 24 without that is drawn as dense housing (I). r2b completed the landuse (all 56 tiles from one state, plus the 59 relations that had been dropped). Belle Air is now 0 % commercial; it had been all slabs. The OSM mask overlays (look1_osm_mask_v2_climb_sweeney.png, look1_osm_mask_low_v1_climb_fwd.png) and the pixel picks put the remaining slabs on OSM polygons such as San Bruno Towne Center, retail way 24570872 north of I-380 and the Bayhill commercial way. The Tanforan caveat is resolved: 93 % commercial by OSM.

Each zone line now carries an arterial (14 m, sidewalks, centre line; I). zoneKeep draws a slab or house only if it lies wholly inside its own zone and clear of the arterial, so no partial wedges remain. crops_look-2.png shows the reviewer's v3 and v1 wedge regions: triangles before, full rectangles after. Not done: a real street network from OSM (open question).

Since r2, OSM carriageways are drawn as vector ribbons in the city bakes (lanes x 3.66 m + shoulders, MUTCD lines, alpha = coverage), replacing the 58.6 m share. r2b root cause of the remaining blots: on I-380 at x -3463 the pavement lay on 25-46 % mesh slopes with N.L < 0, because the DEM smears the fill crown. Fix: the shading normal is level under ribbon coverage, in both renderers. crops_look-3.png shows crisp ribbons and no blots on the pavement. The dark band left beside the ribbons (v2 at -3469, -1754; w3) is the fill's north side slope 5-20 m outside the pavement, real 3DEP geometry in self-shadow under the 11 deg sun. The dark streak in the v2 foreground is a 3-4 m 3DEP embankment at least 360 m from any motorway.

Not a terrain or land-cover defect; reassigned to the environment track, as the reviewer's own suggested fix implies. The controlled A/B (cmp_v2_climb_sweeney_fogAB.png, scene.fogNode = null, same camera, time and METAR) shows Sweeney Ridge as a dark blue-grey forest silhouette without fog: ridge-to-sky luma 0.45, against 0.88 with the aerial-perspective in-scatter. The land-cover palette is right; the near-white comes from in-scatter.

The bare shore band was removed in r2. NLCD 95 marsh has its own Landsat-measured palette, urban stays on developed shore texels, and salt pans and beaches use the NLCD 31 lowland palette. crops_look-5.png (v5) shows the East Bay marsh islands darker and browner than the water, where before they were beige with light rims. In v4 the Burlingame bayfront picks as developed (dev 238) and NLCD 21. The remaining pale tone in that sunward grazing view is in-scatter (see look-4).

Same root cause and fix as truth-r1-T1: a narrow bank that lifts only ground below the water level, plus the gate beyond 60 m. crops_look-6.png (w2_merced, w1_sanandreas) shows no black shore walls or crater rim after the fix. The reviewer's +49.6 m point now matches 3DEP exactly.

Rejected in part. The colour claim is refuted: Landsat 9 SR on Lake Merced/Harding Park turf gives 0.0443/0.0629/0.0355, against the shipped 'green' 0.0481/0.0633/0.0358. The khaki cast is in-scatter (look-4 A/B; with fog the cemetery renders olive-grey). The flatness and the 60-120 m soft edges are the honest limit of the 30 m NLCD class on 58.6 m texels. No observed finer source was available, so no detail was faked. OSM cemetery/park polygons are proposed in open_questions.

Same fix as truth-r1-T6: the fine inner bake gives 2.05 m on high and 4.1 m on phone over the climb and approach corridors. crops_look-8.png shows individual roofs and straight slab and street edges, against the 3.9 m smear before. Not tested in motion.

r2 added a 10 m shoreline refinement, fitted to NAIP inside the box (NAIP used for measurement only) and to 3DEP outside. Flips across the north edge fell from 36 to 20, and the ASCII map shows the channel as continuous water from z -2410 to -2290. The render after_n1_naip_north_edge.png shows no step at z -2350.

Mostly not terrain; the in-scatter goes to the environment track. The A/B cmp_v5_arr_eastbay_fogAB.png shows the front-lit Hayward hills as warm brown relief with canyon detail when the aerial perspective is off (luma stddev 43.0, hills-to-sky 0.70). With it on they are a flat pale band (stddev 10.9, 0.89). The 180 m ring-2 mesh visibly carries the relief, so it is not the cause.

findings.title: The lake bank rule builds a 45 m wide platform at lake level on the downstream side of Crystal Springs Dam. It sits up to 37 m above the 3DEP 1 m ground, and the real crest is drawn 5 to 10 m too low
findings.evidence:
js/world/terrain.js:89 lifts any ground below level + 0.5 m within 45 m of the ring, fading out by 60 m. My lake probe (10 m grid, own point-in-polygon; scratchpad rev3_truth/lakes_probe.mjs) finds the largest lift at Lower Crystal Springs: (1197.8, 9964.1), 46 m from the ring, demY 55.34 lifted to 83.95. That is 94 cells (0.0094 km2), matching the doc.

I took a profile along the ring normal from (1153.7, 9977.4), direction (0.958, -0.288), and queried USGS EPQS at each point (best-available 3DEP at 1 m resolution, acquired 10/2023; rev3_truth/epqs.py). Values are y = NAVD88 - 0.993:
- s = 0: truth 88.73, height() 83.39
- s = 10: truth 93.86 (the crest), height() 84.39
- s = 20: truth 67.91, height() 84.39
- s = 30: truth 54.40, height() 84.39
- s = 40: truth 47.04, height() 84.39 (+37.4 m)
- s = 50: truth 47.04, height() 76.35
- s = 60: truth 47.00, height() 51.32

The drawn mesh is also wrong:
- high (45 m patch): s = 40 is 69.06 (+22.0 m), s = 60 is 63.43 (+16.4 m)
- low: s = 40 is 79.67 (+32.6 m), s = 50 is 77.08 (+30.0 m)

EPQS at 30 of the lifted cells (epqs_lift.py): max +37.1 m, median +12.5 m, 77 % more than 5 m above the 1 m ground. San Andreas Lake (70 cells) is lifted up to +7.4 m (median +3.8 m) above the 1 m ground on the dam's downstream face. The reservoir levels themselves are right: EPQS gives 84.88 and 134.35, the same as the shipped values.

terrain.md §11 and terrain.js:30-34 justify the lift by the 30 m lattice smearing the crest, and say the 1/3" crop was not fetched that far. The source is obtainable: EPQS answered every one of the 53 queries today, and 3DEP tile n38w123 covers the dam. The rule therefore replaces observed terrain with a synthetic plateau where the original data is available.
findings.suggested_fix: Fetch the 1/3" (or 1 m) DEM around both dams. Draw the real crest (about 89.7 to 94.9 m NAVD88 at Crystal Springs) and the downstream face from it, for example as a dam-local fine patch or ring. Restrict the lift to the measured crest footprint instead of a 45 m band. Add a gate comparing height() across both dams with the 1 m values.

findings.title: Over the Bay the traffic floor is the synthetic water bed (-2.6 to -11.6 m), so bodies can be drawn under the water plane and AGL is measured from the bed
findings.evidence:
Terrain.floorAt over Bay water returns meshY, which is the baked bed. With the high and low meshes built at [0, 0] (rev3_truth/floor_water.mjs):
- (2500, 800): -5.68
- (4000, 1500): -8.65
- (6000, 2400): -6.25
- (3000, -2000): -11.60
- On a 50 m grid within 8 km of the ARP, floorAt < 0 at 37.5 % of 103,041 points (min -11.60).

In traffic.js this floor is used everywhere:
- :741/:748 (airborne y = max(y, yF))
- :3094 (ctlAir clamp)
- :2610 (ground y = floorY)

An aircraft whose reported altitude is low or negative over the Bay, or a ground-flagged target there, is therefore drawn up to 11.6 m below the water surface y = 0. Before this branch it was clamped at GROUND_Y 3. AGL for gear and flaps (traffic.js:3162) and for landing lights (app.js:396 altAgl) over water now reads 8.7 to 14.6 m higher than with GROUND_Y. The invariants cannot see this, because vert.below compares with the same floor.
findings.suggested_fix: Where the ground is water (height() < 0 / Bay mask), make the floor max(meshY, 0), the water plane. Add an invariant for y < 0.

findings.title: Inside the flat zone, 0.058 km2 is NAIP Bay water. height() is the bed there but floorAt returns GROUND_Y, and the doc says height() equals GROUND_Y everywhere in F
findings.evidence:
On a 5 m grid over the NAIP coverage (rev3_truth/probe_wet.mjs), 2,324 cells have flatW = 1 and height() < 0. Of these, 1,833 lie inside AIRPORT_LAND_ST and none on pavement. Examples: the bins around (-1720, -2330), (-400, 1810) and (490, -1000).

height() returns the NAIP seawall bed before applying the flat zone (terrain.js height()). floorAt (terrain.js:296) returns GROUND_Y wherever flatW >= 1, so a body there would hover 3 m above water drawn at y < 0.

terrain.md:166 says "k = 1 on F (so height() === GROUND_Y everywhere in F ...)". The gate (check_terrain.mjs, flat_F_20m) only tests F ∩ land.
findings.suggested_fix: Either exclude NAIP water from F's k = 1, or make floorAt check height() < 0 first. Correct the doc wording.

findings.title: terrain.md §6, the modification notice the 3DEP licence (useconst) requires, is out of date, and other doc numbers are stale
findings.evidence:
Stale statements:
- terrain.md:283 (§6 item 1): "the 120 m ring after a Gaussian prefilter of σ 30 m". The shipped value is 15 m: header rings[2].src says "Gaussian prefilter sigma 15 m", rules.r2_prefilter_sigma_m is 15.0, and build_terrain.py:96 sets R2_SIGMA_M = 15.0.
- §6 item 5: "Reservoir and lake beds carved ... banks mirrored". It does not mention the bank lift that raises real ground by up to +28.6 m over the 3DEP ring (Crystal Springs Dam) and +8.3 m (San Andreas). §6 is the only modification notice the tile useconst asks for.
- terrain.md:319 (§8 item 5): "the ≈ 1 m offset documented". This contradicts §3, now 0.14 m.
- terrain.md:340 (§9): low tier 250k. The measured value is 266,287.
- terrain.md:350: sfo_dem.bin 2.42 MB, sfo_landcover.bin 3.17 MB. The rebuild gives 2.46 MB and 3.53 MB.
- terrain.md:364: 742k / 250k vertices and height() 0.17 µs. Measured: 840,230 / 266,287 vertices and 0.236 µs.
- terrain.md:370: phone 250,151 vertices. Measured: 266,287.
findings.suggested_fix: Update §6 (σ 15 m; describe the bank lift and its extent) and refresh §8, §9 and §10 from the r2b build report.

findings.title: There is no disposition report for round 1. T9 and T10 are still unfixed with no recorded rejection
findings.evidence: No REPORT.md exists under scratchpad wf/terrain/r1b, r2 or r2b (find over wf/terrain; only r1b/named.md and r2/inv_compare.md are there). terrain.md §12 says "the dispositions and renders are in the workflow report". The round-1 truth findings T9 and T10 are unchanged in the code and data (see TR2-7 and TR2-8), so it cannot be checked whether they were rejected or overlooked.

findings.title: Two quantitative explanations in the doc do not match the raw data: the cause of the motorway shading and the palette's unfiltered-mean claim
findings.evidence:
(a) Motorway shading. terrain.md:231 says "the 10-30 m DEM lattice and the mesh smear a fill's crown into its side slopes". Measured under the OSM carriageway centrelines in r0 (layer 0, non-link, every 10 m, cross slope over ±5 m; rev3_truth/mw_check.py, mw_mesh.mjs):

| Surface | p50 | > 10 % | > 25 % |
|---|---|---|---|
| raw 3DEP 1/3" | 1.7 % | 0.7 % | 0 % |
| height() | 1.7 % | 1.4 % | — |
| mesh, step 15 | — | 3.8 % | — |
| mesh, step 30 | — | 9.2 % | — |
| vertex-normal estimate (±30 m) | — | 13.7 % | — |

The raw p90 is 3.5 %. So the DEM is level under the carriageways; the steep normals come from the mesh step and the cell-wide normals. The vertical-normal override (ground.js GROUND_FS, three/ground.js:699) also removes longitudinal grades under every ribbon.

(b) Palette. terrain.md:246 says "the unfiltered means differ by ≤ 0.004". My own Landsat SR means (QA bits 1-5 clear, NLCD 3x3 pure, no illumination filter; rev3_truth/palette_check.py) agree within about 0.004 for grass, shrub, tree, marsh and barren lowland. Barren upland does not: 0.1225/0.1074/0.0737 over 1,394 pure pixels, against the shipped 0.1298/0.1124/0.0766 over 479 lit pixels. The quarry box alone reads 0.112 unfiltered against 0.094 lit (1,048 vs 200 px).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct both statements. Optionally compute the ribbon-area normals from height() over a short baseline instead of forcing them vertical.

findings.title: Round-1 T9 is still open: no SOURCES.json records the Overpass endpoints' usage policy or the Planetary Computer terms
findings.evidence:
osm_motorways/SOURCES.json (maps.mail.ru) and osm_landuse/SOURCES.json (ovp.dresel.systems) have no terms entry. The policy is only in a fetch_sources.py comment (lines 96-101).

I fetched the OSM wiki 'Public Overpass API instances' list today:
- dresel: "Free to use, no API key. Limit of 4 parallel queries per IP address ... Please send a User-Agent". It is also listed with "Attic data: no", built from Geofabrik daily extracts.
- maps.mail.ru: "Feel free to use our services in any project ... no requests limitations".

The tool sends User-Agent 'sfo3d-terrain-tool' and issues queries one at a time, which complies. For the landuse, terrain.md §9/§11's "an attic query at that time reproduces it on any Overpass instance" holds only for attic-capable instances, not for the one used.

The Landsat crops came via Microsoft Planetary Computer with SAS tokens (landsat/SOURCES.json 'via'), and the PC terms page is not recorded. Its terms page renders only with JavaScript, so I could not read it. The USGS public-domain FAQ quote itself checks out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add api_terms (page, quote, date) to both OSM SOURCES.json entries and to the Landsat entry.

findings.title: Round-1 T10 is still open: traffic.js says a body at GROUND_Y at Hayward was buried 12 m
findings.evidence: traffic.js:495: "Hayward's field, 52 ft, is y ~14.9 - a body at GROUND_Y was buried 12 m". My bilinear read of the 3DEP 1" at the NASR HWD ARP (37.65893, -122.12174) is 9.62 m NAVD88 (y 8.63). The burial at the ARP is therefore about 5.6 m. The NASR field elevation of 52.1 ft is the highest runway point.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the 3DEP ground value instead.

findings.title: The build_terrain.py header still describes the r1 plane layout
findings.evidence: tools/terrain/build_terrain.py:27 lists the outputs as "... + JSON header + regionA + regionB", with no regionC or mw_* sections. Line 58 says "regionB R shrub (52 + 0.5 x 95) ... B green (21, 81, 82 + 0.5 x 95)". The code now puts marsh in regionC.R, and my plane recomputation matches shrub = class 52 only and green = 21/81/82 only, to within 0.002.

(f) Housing up to Skyline is present: C_sb_sunbehind.png and C_sb_top.png show houses on the San Bruno hills. It disappears into the beige in every into-the-sun view, which is the direction the films look.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. Add a normal or detail map from the 1/3" (and 1") DEM to the 45 m and coarser rings, or extend the 15 m ring along the d_climb corridor to Sweeney and San Bruno Mountain.
2. Review the ambient/IBL ground albedo (a warm 0.30 is far above the real regional albedo of about 0.1) and any grazing specular on natural ground.
3. Validate class colours under the film lighting against the Landsat November SR values the build already uses.

findings.title: The San Mateo-Hayward Bridge (CA-92, about 11 km) is missing from the arrival views over the Bay
findings.evidence:
(a) A_a_bay05.png x0-360 y350-431 (the a_bay film camera at u=0.5). sheets/bridge_a_bay05.png draws in magenta where NLCD 2021 developed pixels cross the Bay (from refimg/a_bay05_nlcd.png): a continuous line from (0,431) to (360,350). The app shows open water there.
(b) A_arr_to_apt.png x480-1280 y437-515 (sheets/bridge_arr_to_apt.png): the line passes about 4-5 km from the camera, and every app pixel column there is a smooth water gradient.
(c) A_arr_eastbay_wide.png, left half, about y380-390.
(d) Back-projection to world (11030, 3791) and (12456, 2793): the shipped land cover has freeway coverage 77-132 and water 255 there, so the data knows the road, but no deck is drawn. The r3 decks cover only the lidar box around I-380/US-101.
(e) In reality the bridge, a long low trestle plus the high-rise span at the Foster City end, is a signature feature of SFO arrivals from the SE. It lies just north of the 28R final track, in frame for a_bay and a_side.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the CA-92 bridge (and the Dumbarton Bridge if it is ever in frame) as deck geometry from OSM bridge=yes ways. Take deck heights from Caltrans / 3DEP lidar class-17 points if the lidar can be fetched with a recorded licence; otherwise list it under open_questions. Record src obs/inf for span heights.

findings.title: The north-field landside area (long-term parking, rental cars, cargo) is drawn as bare tan soil with only parking-aisle outlines
findings.evidence:
(a) D_climb_u0.png x650-1280 y330-650 (crop: crops/u0_tanfield.png), about 30% of the first d_climb frame. It shows a large sand-coloured field (187, 166, 139) with grey aisle lines and no asphalt, cars or buildings. Reference refimg/climb_u0_naip.png (NAIP 2024, reference only) shows the same pixels as asphalt lots packed with cars plus large white-roof buildings; see also naipref/naip_north_field_4m.png around world x -2200..-1700, z -2000..-1300.
(b) Back-projected points (-1867,-1507), (-1819,-1685) and (-1827,-1968) are NLCD 24 with app developed weight 255, so the airport bake overrides the land cover with tan.
(c) D_overview_top.png x590-770 y365-440 (crop: crops/top_airport.png): a tan trapezoid with hard straight edges against the city texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the airport land/bake polygon, fall back to developed or landside pavement (asphalt plus the procedural car lots) wherever NLCD is 23/24 and the static pavement layer has no coverage, instead of the tan 'airport soil'. Coordinate with the static/landside owner, since this sits inside AIRPORT_LAND_ST.

findings.title: The procedural city reads as a tiled lattice: identical grey commercial squares and one straight street-grid orientation over the hills
findings.evidence:
(a) D_climb_u05.png x530-1280 y330-570 and D_climb_u1.png x450-1280 y340-700, both d_climb film frames: 20+ identical flat grey squares on a perfect grid. Back-projected (-3906,-2009), (-3806,-2157), (-3546,-2445): this is the Shops at Tanforan / El Camino / Bayhill area, NLCD 24, commercial share 255. The real site is one large irregular mall roof, parking garages, surface lots and the San Bruno BART station. Also visible in D_climb_sweeney.png x400-1050 y400-560.
(b) C_sb_top.png (whole frame) and C_sb_sunbehind.png: residential rows run in one straight orientation up and over the San Bruno hills. The real hill neighbourhoods (Crestmoor, Rollingwood, Portola Highlands, Mills Park) have curvilinear streets that follow the contours.
(c) E_seawall_south.png x0-1280 y380-720 (Millbrae bayfront by US-101): small houses and a car park. refimg/seawall_south_naip.png and naipref/naip_millbrae_2m.png (NAIP, reference only) show US-101 running diagonally through the foreground and large flat-roof commercial and hotel blocks; the freeway is not legible in the app.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. Vary commercial lot footprint, size, rotation and roof tone; merge adjacent commercial blocks into larger roofs with parking aprons.
2. Orient residential blocks to the local OSM street direction (or the contour direction on slopes > ~8%), not one zone-wide angle.
3. Make sure motorway ribbons draw over commercial and residential bakes near the airport bake rectangle.

findings.title: Aerial perspective is far too strong for the films' 'CLR 10SM' METAR: the airport, the peninsula and the East Bay hills wash out to beige at 5-15 km and Mt Tamalpais never appears (environment-owned, but it decides how the terrain reads)
findings.evidence:
(a) A_arr_to_apt.png x0-460 y310-515: the Foster City / San Mateo shoreline and hills at 5-15 km are nearly sky-coloured, and the airport is invisible. Compare refimg/arr_to_apt_shade.png and refimg/arr_to_apt_nlcd.png.
(b) A_a_bay05.png y260-340 and A_a_side05.png y300-345: the East Bay hills are faint ghosts.
(c) D_climb_u05.png x1100-1280 y125-145: the raw-3DEP skyline there is at 36-37 km (Mt Tamalpais / Marin, cyan line in sheets/cmp_climb_u05_ov.png); the app shows sky.
(d) The METAR group '10SM' is the US upper reporting value ('10 SM or more'), so rendering it as 16 km visibility is an assumption, and a hazy one for a CLR November afternoon. At that density a 0.03-albedo forest at 0.5-1 km is already dominated by in-scatter, which feeds look-r3-1 and look-r3-2.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat 10SM as a lower bound in env/METAR handling (e.g., a documented clear-day meteorological range ≥ 30-50 km when CLR, marked as inferred). Re-render the d_climb and a_bay previews to check that ridges and the East Bay keep contrast.

findings.title: A bright sun-glare plume or light pillar is painted over terrain in downward views, far from the sun direction
findings.evidence:
(a) D_overview_top.png x380-650 y0-330 (crop: crops/top_airport.png context): a glowing white-yellow plume over Sweeney Ridge and the north end of San Andreas Lake that hides the lake. The view axis is pitch 85° toward 270°; the sun is at azimuth 238.6°, elevation 11°, i.e. 70-80° away from the plume pixels.
(b) C_sb_top.png x450-760 y0-520: a vertical smoke-like glow over San Bruno with the camera looking 75° down.
(c) D_overview_high.png x380-560 y0-210 and x350-700 y450-720: vertical light pillars spanning the full frame height, although the sun is above the frame top (frame top is at -7.5°, sun at +11°).
(d) Reference: with the sun 64-80° off-axis, neither Mie forward scatter nor water glint can produce a localized glow of this strength over land. My raw-3DEP renders of the same cameras (refimg/overview_top_*.png, sb_top) are uniform there.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the sun-glare, god-ray or bloom post pass for an off-screen or behind-plane sun projection and clamp it. Check the haze in-scatter phase function for viewing angles toward the ground. Out of terrain scope but visible in every overview.

findings.title: Salt ponds and the Hayward shoreline marsh show as uniform flat olive-khaki islands
findings.evidence: A_arr_eastbay_wide.png x300-1280 y385-445 and A_a_bay05.png x0-1280 y340-410. These are flat, untextured grey-olive shapes with soft edges. refimg/a_bay05_nlcd.png shows a mosaic of NLCD 95/90 wetland and 31 barren (Eden Landing ponds). In reality the ponds are a grid of straight-levee basins whose colour ranges from green to rust or red with the salinity stage.
findings.suggested_fix: Give barren lowland and marsh cells levee lines from OSM (water=salt_pond / man_made=dyke, if licence-clean) and per-pond tint variation; at least add a marsh-vegetation texture.

findings.title: The high overview shows the world's edge: past about 60-75 km the frame top is a bright fog wall, not ocean
findings.evidence: D_overview_high.png x0-1280 y0-230 (camera at 11 km altitude, pitch -30°, vfov 45°, so the frame top is 7.5° below the horizon). The rays there meet the sea about 80 km out, beyond the 61 km rings and water plane; the app paints a uniform haze wall. refimg/overview_high_nlcd.png shows ocean or land to the frame top.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the water plane and a low-detail ring (or a sea-level skirt) to at least the overview camera's horizon distance, or cap overview altitude or pitch.

findings.title: QA/spot cameras placed low with a long target distance clip the airfield at the near plane, showing the Bay water plane (with glitter) through the ground
findings.evidence: C_g_west.png, C_g_sw.png, C_g_eastend_w.png and A_g_sw_hills.png, all y525-670: a camera-centred speckled band. The camera sits 3 m above GROUND_Y with dist 2000, so js/live/controls.js camera() sets near = clamp(0.008*dist) = 16 m. The ground is clipped 8-16 m in front, and the y=0 water plane 3 m below shows through. The in-app UI cannot reach this (pitch ≥ 2°), and the films' telephoto spot cameras do not frame that far below the horizon, but QA or spot cameras can.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the near plane by the camera height above ground (e.g., near ≤ 0.5·(camY - groundY)), or let QA look() pass an explicit near plane.
